mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 3 Series 316 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 3 Series 316 engine replacement typically costs between £1,500 and £6,500 depending on the engine code and condition type. A used N47D20C for the F30 316d starts from around £1,800, while a fully rebuilt unit with warranty ranges from £4,500-£6,500. Petrol N43 engines are cheaper - used units from £400, rebuilt from £2,000-£3,200. Specialist fitting adds £650-£910 in labour.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 3 Series 316d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning sign is a rattling noise from the engine on cold start - often described as a 'diesel rattle' that lasts 1-2 seconds before quietening down. As the chain stretches further, you may notice a loss of power, a check engine light, or rattling that persists when the engine is warm. If ignored, the chain can snap, causing catastrophic engine damage.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 3 Series 316?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the value of your car and the extent of the damage. For a 2012-2015 F30 316d worth £4,500-£10,000, a rebuilt engine at £4,500-£5,800 is a significant investment but can be worthwhile if the rest of the car is in good condition and you plan to keep it. For an older E90 316i worth under £4,000, replacement often exceeds the vehicle's value - in these cases, a used engine or scrapping the car may be more economical.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 316d and 318d engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the 316d and 318d use the same 2.0-litre diesel engine block - N47D20 or B47D20 - but with different ECU mapping. The 316d produces 116hp, while the 318d produces 143hp (pre-LCI) or 150hp (LCI). The hardware is essentially identical; the power difference is software-controlled. This means replacement engines for the 316d and 318d are often interchangeable, but always verify compatibility with your specific VIN.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 3 Series 316 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 3 Series 316 engine replacement typically takes 2-3 days for a specialist workshop to complete, assuming the replacement engine is already in stock with the supplier. The labour time for the F30 316d is approximately 10-14 hours, while the E90 316i is slightly quicker at 8-10 hours. Supply-only delivery usually takes 1-3 working days depending on your location.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between reconditioned, rebuilt and used BMW 316 engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Used engines are taken directly from donor vehicles - they're the cheapest option but come with unknown mileage and history. Reconditioned engines are professionally cleaned, tested, and have worn components replaced - they offer a good balance of cost and reliability. Rebuilt engines are fully stripped, cleaned, machined, and reassembled with new parts including pistons, rings, bearings and gaskets - they're the most expensive but come with a 12-month warranty and are the closest you'll get to a new engine.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 3 Series 316 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 316 has served as the entry-level 3 Series since the E21 generation of the 1970s, evolving from a carburettor-fed 1.6-litre four-cylinder to a turbocharged 2.0-litre diesel. Across its history, the 316 badge has been applied to both petrol and diesel engines spanning five chassis generations.

milestones.description: 1994 (E30) - M40B16, 1.6-litre petrol, 100hp - single overhead cam, fuel-injected
2005 (E46) - N42B18 / N46B16, 1.6-litre petrol, 115hp - Valvetronic, double VANOS
2012 (E90) - N43B16A, 1.6-litre petrol, 122hp - direct injection, no turbo
2019 (F30 LCI) - B47D20A, 2.0-litre diesel, 116hp - replaced N47 with revised timing chain design

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 3 Series 316 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 3 Series 316 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 316 has worn many different engines over five decades, but the majority of replacement-intent searches today come from owners of the N47- and B47-powered F30 316d. The N47 timing chain crisis has created a massive secondary market for replacement engines, while N43 petrol 316i owners face their own set of reliability challenges. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: N47 Timing Chain Failure - Why the BMW 3 Series 316d N47 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The N47's timing chain is mounted at the rear of the engine, making it labour-intensive to access. The original tensioner design allows the chain to stretch and slacken, causing it to rub against and destroy the plastic guides. Debris from the guides falls into the oil sump and blocks the oil pickup, starving the engine of oil.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New chain, tensioner, guides - oil pan drop required to clear debris
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early (cold-start rattle only, no loss of power)
When chain has snapped or engine has seized - most cost-effective route

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2012-2015 F30 316d is worth approximately £4,500-£10,000 `[THIRD-PARTY]`. At the lower end of this band, a full rebuilt engine replacement may represent 60-80% of the vehicle's value - making used or reconditioned engines a more financially sensible option. At the higher end, a rebuilt unit with warranty is a sound investment if you plan to keep the car for 2+ years.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the engine on cold start, get the timing chain inspected immediately. A £1,200-£1,800 specialist chain replacement is far cheaper than a £4,000-£6,000 engine replacement. If the chain has already snapped, a rebuilt engine through a specialist is typically better value than a main dealer replacement - often saving £2,000+ while still including a 12-month warranty.

problems.group: N43 Petrol Timing Chain Guide Failure
problems.h4: N43 Petrol Timing Chain Guide Failure - Why the BMW 3 Series 316i N43 Fails
problems.rootCause: The N43's timing chain guides are made of plastic that becomes brittle over time. When they break, fragments drop into the sump and block the oil pump intake, causing oil starvation and potential engine seizure. The chain itself rarely breaks - it's the guide debris that kills the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New chain, guides, tensioner - oil pan drop and debris removal
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught before engine seizure
When engine has seized or guides have caused catastrophic damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2007-2012 E90 316i is worth approximately £2,500-£6,000 `[THIRD-PARTY]`. At the lower end, replacement cost often exceeds vehicle value - evaluate scrap value before committing. At the higher end, a rebuilt engine may be viable if the car is in excellent condition otherwise.
problems.recommendation: The N43 is a high-maintenance engine. If you're experiencing misfires, loss of power, or rattling from the timing chain area, have a specialist inspect it immediately. If the engine has seized, compare the cost of a rebuilt unit against the vehicle's market value - in many cases, it may be more economical to sell the car for parts and buy another.
